- scripts/claude_issue_route.py:1557-1558 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The pickup reads all pending target issues upfront in one batch (`fetch_dispatch_targets(result["pending"])` in `_cmd_queue_pending`), then creates sessions sequentially. If `ai:claude` is removed after the batch-read but before that issue's `create_session` call, the target stays pending and the pickup starts the session anyway.
  WHY: `.claude/commands/implement-issue-claude.md` step 2 line 18 ("add `ai:claude` if missing") re-adds the label and proceeds, defeating the park; the interval between batch read and the last session start can stretch to minutes.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Removing `ai:claude` from a queued issue now stops the Claude issue pickup from starting it. Before it starts one, it re-reads the target issue (one REST read per item started, #6057). If the issue was closed, lost its `ai:claude` claim, or gained `ai:codex` since it was queued, the pickup starts nothing for it and closes the queue item as not planned."
  Expected change site: scripts/claude_issue_route.py:1555-1567 (the `_cmd_queue_pending` `fetch_dispatch_targets` batch call) together with .claude/commands/implement-issue-claude.md:18 (the unconditional re-add of `ai:claude`).
  Evidence of absence: The implementation reads every pending target issue once, up front, in `fetch_dispatch_targets(result["pending"])` before the loop (scripts/claude_issue_route.py:1557); the pickup then creates sessions sequentially via claude-issue-dispatch.md step 2, which itself never re-reads the issue (its step 2 calls `create_session` directly with the URL, with no `repos/<repo>/issues/<N>` GET). If `ai:claude` is removed between the batch read and the `create_session` call for that entry, the new session starts and .claude/commands/implement-issue-claude.md:18 re-adds the label, so the parked issue still starts. The progress log's own [source:plan-deviation] lesson (docs/implement-plan/issue-6057-recheck-claude-label-at-dispatch.md:46) acknowledges this exact gap: "A gate that must hold 'at dispatch time' needs a read at the moment of dispatch: checking only where the payload is first validated (the intake) leaves every later state change of the target invisible to the session starter." The Copilot review comment (id 4166007448, posted 2026-10-02T13:09:29Z on the fixed head 9d6cbf9, after round 1) flags this exact race: ".claude/commands/implement-issue-claude.md:18 adds it back when the new session reaches its gate, so the parked issue still starts. Add a final session-side check that stops when the live claim is absent (rather than re-adding it), or otherwise make claim validation part of the launch handoff." The autofix commit (2ce9fd27) only modified the handoff failure-path telemetry, the test assertions, and the progress log text; it did not add a per-session re-check and did not change the implementation session's re-add. As a result the PR's headline claim holds only against label changes that arrive more than seconds before the pickup's wake.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

  WHY: The pickup starts pending entries sequentially, while `.claude/commands/implement-issue-claude.md` step 2 adds `ai:claude` when it is missing instead of stopping. Removing the label during that interval therefore does not prevent the session from proceeding.

  PROBLEM: The claim check is not part of the session-start handoff. If `ai:claude` is removed after the pickup's batch read but before the implementation session's step 2 runs, the session re-adds the label and proceeds, defeating the park.
  WHY: The pickup reads all pending targets in one batch call (line 1558), then the pickup command sequentially creates sessions via `claude-issue-dispatch.md` step 2. With the default limit of 20 targets, the interval between the first read and the last session start can be minutes. The PR's headline claim — "Removing `ai:claude` from an issue that is already queued now stops the Claude issue pickup from starting it" — holds only against label changes that arrive more than seconds before the pickup's wake. The progress log's Lessons section acknowledges this tension ("A gate that must hold 'at dispatch time' needs a read at the moment of dispatch") but no code change implements the fix.

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Removing `ai:claude` from an issue that is already queued now stops the Claude issue pickup from starting it." (PR description headline). The pickup re-reads each target and refuses it, but the implementation session that the pickup starts re-adds `ai:claude` if missing, so a target parked between the pickup's batch read and the session's start still proceeds.
  Expected change site: `.claude/commands/implement-issue-claude.md` step 2 "Claim" (line 18), which currently says "add `ai:claude` if missing"; or the pickup's per-entry session-start path in `.claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md` step 3, which would need a final re-check before `create_session`.
  Evidence of absence: `fetch_dispatch_targets` in `scripts/claude_issue_route.py:943-980` reads all pending targets up front in one batch (`fetch_dispatch_targets(result["pending"])` at line 1557), then the pickup creates sessions sequentially. `.claude/commands/implement-issue-claude.md:18` reads the issue in step 1, then in step 2 "Claim" unconditionally adds `ai:claude` if missing and proceeds — it does not stop when the label is absent. So if `ai:claude` is removed after the pickup's batch read but before the session's step 2, the session re-adds the label and continues implementation. The `codex_label_added` and `issue_closed` cases are fully handled (step 2 "Routed away" and "Closed" gates stop the session), but the `claude_label_removed` case is not. The PR's own lesson in the progress log acknowledges this: "A gate that must hold 'at dispatch time' needs a read at the moment of dispatch." No code change implements that lesson on the session side. The file is not in the PR's declared scope (it has no `workflow-templates/.claude/` twin, so under the interim twin-first rule it cannot be edited in this PR), but the PR's headline claim is not fully met without it.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
